problem: The text says point clouds have no normals and that a meshing step is needed before ordinary rendering. Many laser scanners and depth pipelines output per-point normals, and point clouds are commonly rendered directly as point or splat primitives without any meshing.
fix: Point clouds are unordered lists of 3D points with no faces and usually no connectivity. Some scanners also output a normal per point. They can be drawn directly as points or splats, or converted to a mesh when a surface is needed.

problem: "Both numbers lie between 0 and 1" is only true for the base tile. UV values outside [0, 1] are normal and are used to repeat or tile a texture across a surface; the statement as written would make tiling look impossible.
fix: In the base mapping u and v run from 0 to 1 across the image, whatever its size in pixels. Values outside that range are allowed and select a repeated copy of the image (tiling).

problem: Tessellation by itself only subdivides a polygon; it does not round a curved silhouette. The rounding comes from the curved surface definition used with the subdivision (for example PN triangles or Phong tessellation) or from a displacement map.
fix: Tessellation splits a coarse polygon into smaller triangles, giving more vertices to work with. When it is combined with a curved surface rule such as PN triangles, the silhouette of a curved object becomes rounder and detail can be added near the camera.
